text:
maria: Quick check — Acme Corp asked us to remove traces and cached responses for org_id=acme-118. What is the minimal set we can delete that won't break debugging or alerts? Who needs to approve this?
aj: We don't have an ad-hoc erase path for traces AFAIK. For one-off customer requests we typically need product + legal + eng-security approvals. Also confirm which environments (prod vs staging).
jen: For caches (redis) we can evict org-scoped keys. For traces: raw blobs in S3 + any indexes. Deleting blobs is straightforward; index pruning needs care.
samir: Quick find command I've used (DO NOT RUN without approvals):
```
redis-cli --scan --pattern "resp:org:acme-118:*" | xargs -n1 redis-cli del
```
That clears response cache entries. Trace blobs live in s3 under traces/acme-118/ then timestamped folders.
maria: Good to know. What's the formal approval flow? Is filing a ticket enough or do we need a board sign-off?
sec-bot: @maria Please submit a Data Erasure Request in the internal portal: https://internal.redwood/erase. Attach the customer's request, org id, and the requested scope. Required approvers: product-owner, legal, eng-security. The deletion will be audited automatically.
aj: Also note: traces are two-layered — blobs (S3) and the search index (ES). Removing blobs will stop storage cost and content access; the ES index must be pruned or reindexed to avoid dangling pointers. That prune should be scheduled during a low-traffic window.
jen: I can run the ES index prune and the cache evict. Need eng-security sign-off and a scheduled maintenance window. Prefer tonight 02:00 UTC; I'll stage on staging first and prepare rollback steps.
maria: I'll open the portal ticket now and attach the customer email. Will ping here once approvers are on it. Thanks everyone :+1:
